text: alice.chen: Heads-up — found a vuln in the Feature Flags UI. Rendering endpoint for flag description (/api/v1/flags/:id/preview) reflects unsanitized markdown titles. I can get script execution in org-admin console if a non-admin flag name contains . alice.chen: quick PoC (repro on staging): ```bash curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/api/v1/flags -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"name":"","project_id":"proj_123"}' ``` opens the admin flags page and pops the alert. raj.patel: yikes. is this reflected or stored? alice.chen: stored in flags table, rendered server-side into the preview HTML without proper sanitization. It looks DOM XSS in the admin SPA when previewing flags. tom.kim: who can create flags in prod? should be restricted to org_admins only. any authz bypass too? alice.chen: here's the kicker — the API filter for toggle/create checks `roles CONTAINS 'admin'` but a recent change to RBAC middleware uses `roles LIKE` and a malformed role claim (e.g., roles: "org_admin;user") allowed creation. So two issues: stored XSS + weak RBAC check. maya.gomez: if non-admins can create flags + stored XSS, they can get admin UI context and perform actions as admin via the console? we need to assume privilege escalation. raj.patel: mitigation plan — immediate: 1) throttle/disable public flag creation endpoint, 2) add WAF rule to block requests with angle brackets in name, 3) patch RBAC middleware to use exact-set membership check, 4) sanitize/escape HTML on render and add CSP. Also add audit log entries for flag create/toggle with identity claims. alice.chen: agreed. I'll open a hotfix PR for sanitizer and exact role check. Patch will be minimal: use our `sanitizeMarkdown()` util prior to saving and change `roles LIKE` -> `roles_contains_exact(role)` in middleware. deploy-bot: deployment queued: hotfix/flags-xss-rbac -> rollout (canary 10%) tom.kim: before deployment, let's do containment: disable flag create for non-admins by feature-flagging the endpoint (or config flag) and rotate any long-lived tokens that could exploit RBAC. Raj can you add a quick WAF signature to block `<` and `>` in name param? raj.patel: on it. WAF rule pushed to edge in ~5m. Also adding temporary nginx rewrite to return 403 if name param matches /[<>]/. olivia.lewis: are customers affected / do we need to notify? any PII exposure? alice.chen: no PII observed. This is an XSS + authz vector limited to org spaces where a user could create a flag. We should treat as high-risk because of admin UI context. Recommend holding an external comms draft if we see evidence of exploitation. maya.gomez: I'll prep comms template but hold until we confirm mitigation. Also add to security incident tracker and set severity = P2->P1 if exploit seen. alice.chen: I've added audit logging to capture `flags.create` and `flags.toggle` with full caller claim and request_id. Also logging KMS usage for API token decryption (reference key: projects/api-keys) in case we need key rotation audit. raj.patel: regression test plan: add unit + e2e for sanitizeMarkdown on flag names, add RBAC unit tests for exact role matching, and add an integration test that posts a malicious name and verifies it is escaped in preview HTML. tom.kim: timeline? we need hotfix out asap and then a full patch. Who's owning the incident? alice.chen: I'll own incident until handoff. Hotfix PR ready (alice/flags-hotfix), needs review + CI. Expect canary -> full rollout in ~30m after WAF. raj.patel: WAF and nginx rule live. Blocking ~120 suspicious staging requests already. deploy-bot: canary passed (10%), rolling to 100% in 15m alice.chen: just ran quick smoke: preview no longer executes script, markup is escaped to "<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>". RBAC check updated to strict match. olivia.lewis: thanks. I'll monitor CSM tickets and flag any customer reports. maya.gomez: incident ticket created: INC-2026-114 (security). please attach PR + reproducer. I'll draft internal blurb for execs. tom.kim: post-incident actions: 1) add CSP & X-Content-Type-Options to admin UI, 2) tighten RBAC middleware to use verified role claims from authn service, 3) add automated alerts when sensitive endpoints see non-admin create/toggle activity, 4) run org-wide sweep for other endpoints rendering markdown. alice.chen: will follow up with a short postmortem and remediation checklist. current status: mitigations deployed, WAF active, hotfix rolled to prod, monitoring for anomalies enabled. raj.patel: I'll schedule a post-deploy audit and add new detection rule to our SIEM for `flags.create` events from non-admin principals. alice.chen: thanks all. tagging @maya.gomez for comms and @raj.patel for ops. marking this thread resolved for now; will update INC-2026-114 with final postmortem once done. :white_check_mark:
